note: The National Credit Regulations, regulation 17, as Acts Online publishes it: a consumer's payment profile may be displayed five years; an adverse classification one year, a further listing the game doesn't model. Read in Acts Online's copy, registered as secondary. No source read states how many days after its due date a missed payment is reported, so the days are the game's reading: the bureau's next monthly update. Re-read 2026-11-03: the Government Gazette of 13 March 2015 (No. 38557, as the National Credit Regulator publishes it) replaced regulation 17 with the table Acts Online gives: a payment profile five years from the event. The fact is found on the gazette and Acts Online's copy is no longer cited.

sources.title: Government Gazette No. 38557, Regulation Gazette No. 10382, 13 March 2015: National Credit Regulations including Affordability Assessment Regulations (GN R202), as the National Credit Regulator publishes it
sources.said: Amendment of Regulation 17 of the Regulations Regulation 17 is hereby deleted and replaced with new Regulation 17 as below: Retention periods for credit bureau information (1) The consumer credit information as per the following table must be displayed and used for purposes of credit scoring or credit assessment for a maximum period from the date of the event, as indicated: ... 3. Payment Profile | Factual information pertaining to the payment profile of the consumer | 5 years ... 4. Adverse classifications of ... | 1 year or within the period ...
